messages:
maya: Heads-up: premerge CI for service-auth PR #8451 surfaced a batch of SAST findings and one DAST proof that looks like a transient secret exposure. Artifact: gs://ci/8451/scan.json

trent: can you paste the important bits?

maya: sure — snippet from the CI artifact:
```
SAST: auth/token_manager.go:120 - use of keystore.Decrypt on user-provided key -> rule RDX-KMS-009
DAST: GET /internal/metrics -> response body contains 'db_pass: ****' and shows expansion evidence
```

lucas: tagging @evelyn from infra — any recent RBAC grants or KMS changes for the metrics reader?

evelyn: we added a temporary rollout grant to metrics-reader last Friday for a canary. It should be read-only; no Decrypt permission should have been added. I'll pull the keystore audit slice.

pm-kate: adding context — this PR changes how token_manager falls back to env keys when keyID param is missing. Could be the code path that calls Decrypt incorrectly.

security-bot: Automated summary: 1 HIGH (possible secret exposure), 4 MED (improper keystore usage). Suggested triage: assign owner, reproduce in staging, attach KMS audit logs, update SDLC review checklist if needed.

oncall-sre: I'm available to repro in staging and capture ephemeral grant logs if we need to test old key behavior.

trent: I'll own the SAST side and audit the token_manager code. maya, can you open a ticket and attach the artifact/audit links?

maya: opened RED-9123 and linked the CI artifact. Added initial triage checklist and asked for the keystore audit slice. https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RED-9123

evelyn: attached keystore audit entries for the last 72h to RED-9123. I also found a short-lived grant that accidentally included decrypt: grant id G-7792, created 2025-03-11T02:12Z by deployer-ci. Logging entry included.

lucas: that explains how the metrics reader could surface decrypted config. Code-wise token_manager.go line 118 shows fallback to envKey when keyID=="" and it calls keystore.Decrypt(envKey) without verifying caller identity.

trent: code snippet for reference:
```
// token_manager.go
func RetrieveSecret(keyID, envKey string) (string, error) {
  if keyID == "" {
    return keystore.Decrypt(envKey)
  }
  return keystore.Get(keyID)
}
```
This violates the principle of fail-closed and mixes configuration with runtime decryption. I'll open PR to require explicit keyID and deny Decrypt on health/metrics endpoints.

pm-kate: can we also add an SDLC gate so any Decrypt call triggers a manual security review and an automated RBAC check? It's been missed in recent reviews.

security-bot: Suggestion: add a premerge policy rule (PLCY-KMS-01) that flags any use of keystore.Decrypt in services reachable from unauthenticated or low-privilege routes.

oncall-sre: repro notes: I recreated the ephemeral grant G-7792 in a short sandbox and confirmed GET /internal/metrics returned a partially-decrypted string only during the grant window. Audit shows requestor was deployer-ci pipeline.

maya: action items added to RED-9123: trent -> SAST fix PR (require explicit keyID + fail closed), lucas -> DAST repro and ingress guard, evelyn -> keystore RBAC rollback and keystore-change doc update, pm-kate -> update SDLC review checklist + add PLCY-KMS-01 proposal, oncall-sre -> attach ephemeral grant audit proof. ETA 24h for initial fixes.

trent: opening WIP PR https://github.com/redwood/auth/pull/1055 with test that rejects empty keyID and adds linter annotation so SAST will catch future uses.

lucas: for DAST mitigation I added a runtime ingress guard to surface-only safe config fields and to explicitly redact decrypted secrets from /internal/* endpoints. Deployed as a hotfix to staging.

evelyn: rolled back grant G-7792 and updated the keystore-change playbook to require ticket reference and two approvers for any grant that includes decrypt. Added a snippet to the playbook on how to query keystore audit logs and correlate them to CI artifacts.

pm-kate: I'll work with security on adding PLCY-KMS-01 to the premerge policy set and update the PR checklist to require keystore usage justification.

security-bot: Reminder: any RBAC/KMS grant must be recorded in keystore-change log with ticket reference and the audit slice attached to the milestone.

oncall-sre: ephemeral grant test window closed; audit exported to RED-9123.

maya: DAST re-run in staging shows metrics endpoint no longer exposes decrypted fragments. SAST scan on the PR now passes for RDX-KMS-009. I marked RED-9123 for verification.

trent: merging PR after one more code review; will also add a unit test that simulates a missing keyID and expects an error.

lucas: follow-up: propose we add a lightweight runtime sanitizer library to the dev-deps so teams can opt-in to safe redaction helpers. I'll open RFC.

pm-kate: good idea. Let's put the RFC on the next platform sync. Also planning a short retro to update the security review workflow — aim to reduce these misses.

security-bot: Thread archived to RED-9123. Recommended follow-ups: add PLCY-KMS-01, update keystore-change playbook, add linter rule for keystore.Decrypt usage.

maya: thanks team — closing this slack thread. We'll keep RED-9123 open until postmortem and policy changes are in place. :white_check_mark:
